status: FROZEN BEFORE ANY REAL DATA EXISTS. Changing any value changes the file digest pinned in identity_probe.py and fails the test; a new version file is required instead.
question: Does the vendor response (TICKERS rows plus ACTIONS rows for a probe sample) actually contain the historical identity intervals needed to reconstruct point-in-time membership, so that raw rows should be RETAINED, or must the universe be restricted under an explicit scope amendment?
decision_rule: RETAIN_RAW_INTERVALS if and only if ALL of: (1) issuers_in_sample >= min_issuers_in_sample; (2) identity_change_cases >= min_identity_change_cases (so the absence of failures is not vacuous); (3) the count of issuers carrying any blocking label is exactly 0. Otherwise SCOPE_AMENDMENT. There is no third outcome: an insufficient or unusual response fails closed.

definitions.interval: [firstpricedate, lastpricedate]; a row with isdelisted false and no lastpricedate is open-ended
definitions.overlap: two intervals share at least one calendar day
definitions.TICKER_CHANGE_CURRENT_ONLY: an identity change is evidenced (a second ticker string in the rows for the issuer, or an ACTIONS row whose action contains change_action_substring and whose ticker or contraticker is one of the issuer's tickers) but the TICKERS rows give only ONE ticker interval for that issuer
definitions.SUCCESSOR_IDENTITY_RESOLVED: one ticker string is carried by two or more permatickers whose intervals do not overlap and each of which has both dates
definitions.INTERVAL_GAP_EXPLAINED: consecutive intervals of one issuer are more than gap_days_threshold apart and an ACTIONS row of the issuer dates inside the gap
definitions.AMBIGUOUS_MAPPING: intervals overlap for one ticker across different permatickers, or for one permaticker across different tickers

not_established_by_this_probe: SIP intraday coverage of delisted names; adjustment semantics; licence to retain; any strategy result.
